ticket: T07 — durable runtime, crash protocol, session lifecycle (R04)
finding: the live path held everything in memory. A restart lost the bar accumulators, the volume baselines, the filter state and every decision since start-up, and there was no cursor, so a restart could not know which inputs it had already consumed.

the_transaction.concurrency: the writer states the head version it expected; a mismatch raises HeadConflict and nothing is applied
the_transaction.replay: a repeat of a decision_id returns the stored decision and does NOT advance the head — a crash between commit and acknowledgement must not double-decide
the_transaction.blob_ordering: the state blob is written to a temp file, fsynced and atomically renamed BEFORE the row that names it, so a committed reference always points at a complete file

crash_injection.method: a real sqlite3.Connection subclass passed as the connection factory, failing on one statement. Not a mock of the store — a test that stubs what it checks proves only that the stub works
crash_injection.result: at every point: no decision, head still at 0, no outbox row

verified: a committed decision and its payload hash survive
the restored service keeps its ECDF observation counts
the restored filter state is identical
a replayed pass does not double-decide and the head does not move
bars finalized before the restart stay finalized and re-recording them is a no-op
the bar watermark survives: a late tick cannot reopen a finalized window across the restart
an undelivered outbox event outlives the process

rules_enforced: an illegal transition raises rather than landing somewhere nothing expects
a session is closed only from draining_session: the feed is polled out first, because a late tick for the final bar is the normal case
the drain window is measured from the LAST TICK, so a feed still delivering keeps the session open
degraded keeps running and refuses to publish, and needs a reason
a reconnect does not pass through warmup — it must not look like a cold start
in-memory history is bounded (deque, 200); the durable history is the decision table

calendar_defect_fixed.what: MarketClock.next_open took the day's FIRST window only, so during the lunch gap of a two-window special session it reported the market shut until the next day

entry_point.--status: reads the store, the lifecycle and the clock. Connects to no feed and starts no job, answered before anything is built
entry_point.--once: a BOUNDED WAIT for one finalized batch with an explicit timeout, not connect-and-immediately-poll. On timeout it says how long it waited, the market state and the next open
entry_point.observed: --once --replay timed out honestly after 8s: 'market is not_a_session; next open 2026-10-19T09:15:00+05:30', with the lifecycle in `degraded` because no live feed exists

not_claimed: NO LIVE FEED. The durable path has never run against a real tick stream; every pass so far is a replay or a fixture.
delivery is AT-LEAST-ONCE with a receiver idempotency key. Exactly-once network delivery is not claimed and is not achievable by a store alone.
no delivery transport is attached, so the outbox accumulates and dead-letters after bounded retries (T15).
a PostgreSQL adapter preserving the same repository contract is not built; SQLite is the runtime boundary today.
